Complaint Number: 4002026009197
Incident Date: 05/26/2026

Page 2 of 4
Description:
I am writing to formally request a review of the professional conduct and clinical practices of Kenneth Emeka Ezenwa, NP (License #95080178) regarding a telehealth encounter on May 26, 2026. This submission focuses on Mr. Ezenwa's clinical performance and adherence to the Nursing Practice Act. Please note that a related administrative privacy complaint is currently under review by the OCR (Ticket #[Redacted]72).

Professional Conduct and Clinical Oversight Issues:

Failure to Review Clinical History: At the start of our appointment, Mr. Ezenwa stated he had no access to my medication history or records. He remained unprepared to proceed until I offered to read him the dates from my personal CURES report, which necessitated him placing me on hold to contact his office. This indicates a significant failure to review patient records prior to providing clinical services.

Improper Prescribing and Overriding Patient Boundaries: During the encounter, I explicitly communicated that I was in the process of a "warm hand-off" for my Diazepam taper from my current provider and clearly declined the addition of Sertraline. Mr. Ezenwa repeatedly refused to accept this boundary, persisting in his demand for the medication until I ultimately consented solely to end the circular and unproductive exchange. This behavior reflects a disregard for patient boundaries and a failure to engage in the collaborative, informed decision-making required by the Nursing Practice Act. My pharmacy records confirm this prescribing activity, which occurred despite my clear, documented objections during the appointment.

Substandard Administrative Environment: The appointment was characterized by a chaotic communication breakdown, involving multiple overlapping calls from clinic lines during the scheduled telehealth window. This prevented a professional clinical environment and impeded my ability to access care.

Request for Action:
I request that the Board investigate Mr. Ezenwa's adherence to the Nursing Practice Act regarding record-keeping requirements, the maintenance of professional clinical standards, and the appropriate use of his prescribing (furnishing) authority.
